newsitem.title: DUBAI: Tehran refinery workers protest over pay.
newsitem.headline: Tehran refinery workers protest over pay.

text.p: Workers from a major Iranian refinery on Sunday held demonstrations inside the oil ministry protesting against low wages before agreeing to go back to work, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said.
IRNA did not say if work had come to a halt at the Tehran refinery, the country's third largest, with a capacity of 225,000 barrels per day.
The agency said "tens" of workers shouted slogans supporting Iranian spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and called on the oil ministry to agree to their wage demands.
Representatives of the workers then held negotiations with oil ministry officials.

One of the representatives said the protesters had reached an agreement with ministry officials and would return to work in the next few hours, IRNA said. The agency did not give details of the demands or the agreement reached.
